newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Bergsten-Currencies can't keep weakening vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bergsten-Currencies can't keep weakening vs dlr.

text.p: European currencies and the yen cannot keep weakening against the dollar at a time U.S. current account deficits are widening while surpluses in other countries are rising, economist C. Fred Bergsten said.

Bergsten, director of the Institute for International Economics, told the World Economic Forum in Davos that calls for competitive devaluation from Japan and European countries were understandable given weak domestic economies in those countries.
"There is a fundamental disconnect in the financial markets," Bergsten added.

"The currency of the country with the largest debt and deficits is rising sharply against all currencies. The currencies of countries with the largest surpluses and creditor positions are declining substantially. It is a situation that cannot continue and will be resversed," he said.
Bergsten also called for the Group of Seven countries to adopt a yen stabilisation pact at their meeting next week to prevent a sharp decline in the Japanese currency.

He cited the risk of a vicious circle in which a drop in Japanese stocks could drive investors out of yen which would in turn drive investors out of Japanese shares, putting in place a "sell Japan panic" that could provoke severe reactions in foreign markets as well.
